claim: A young man asks whether others, in their second to third week of retaining, hit a phase of feeling bad about themselves and their progress and just feel like releasing. He learned somewhere that this is when unhealed traumas and inner child problems arise: is it true, and how to deal with it, since it can be hard and overwhelming, especially alone?

Working on this stuff (unhealed traumas, inner child problems, the emotions that come up in retention) takes so much courage, and so does reaching out for support and aligning with other guys working on it
name: Community and accountability

claim: Don't get too hung up on the time frame of the emotional wall in retention: it may happen at any point, probably around a week for a lot of guys starting out, or a month or two in for those practicing that long; maybe why one listener hits it at two to three weeks

In retention, probably the easy way to call a phase of feeling bad and just feeling like releasing is "a bit of an emotional wall", kind of hit in some way after maybe feeling great, better and better
Hitting an emotional wall in retention: "It is very, very common" at various stages of retention
For a lot of guys in the beginning of retention, the wall is an overwhelm of sexual energy, of uncontrolled lust
A wall of feeling bad about yourself and your progress in retention is a little bit different from an overwhelm of sexual energy, and very, very important

Do unhealed traumas and inner child problems arise in retention? "I would say absolutely one of the things that will happen as you practice retention": you dive deeper into yourself, your power, life force and emotions, so you'll hit points where you get a little uncomfortable and emotions you haven't really tapped into before

Hitting uncomfortable points and emotions you haven't tapped into before in retention is to be expected: experienced personally, and seen "over and over and over again with guys", one listener being an example, along with many clients and others heard from
For a lot of guys, retention is practiced essentially alone, so the emotional wall can feel very alone and unsure
Suggested approach to the emotional wall in retention: base it on a lot of introspection
In introspection, ask what you feel uncomfortable about, what emotions come up, in what area of life
name: Emotions

claim: Introspection is the foundation of understanding and awareness, "And it's the awareness that's key."
name: Emotions

claim: "Releasing" is a key word: ejaculation is in fact a huge energetic release, often thought of, maybe not negatively (though sometimes it's easy to fall into that trap), but as draining
Ejaculation is also a powerful potential release of things we want to let go of

Through introspection (meditating, thinking, journaling, talking to a close friend), once clearly aware of something you really need to let go of, an intentional release aimed at letting it go "can be incredibly powerful"
With clear awareness of something you need to let go of and a clear intention, you'll very likely experience a lot of positive benefits from an intentional release
Our emotions, all our trauma and inner child stuff, live in our body
name: Emotions

claim: Emotions living in the body is one reason we hit the emotional wall in retention in different ways, times and layers, tapping more strongly into the life force there
Since our emotions live in our body, a physical release can serve a hugely positive role; the difference is awareness
Retention is not about never releasing, nor about seeing a release as a bad thing, "because it's not"
Too many releases will drag you down; unconscious ones, without intention, discipline or awareness, probably will
An aware, intentional release at the right time for the right reasons can be incredibly powerful and beneficial
At the emotional wall, releasing won't always necessarily be the best call, and there's not a right or wrong: "it's all testing and learning"

At the emotional wall, sometimes the work is to keep pushing against retention while working through emotions in other ways, probably especially without clarity about what to let go of, or when it isn't deep and longstanding, not stress from work yesterday
With awareness of deeper things to let go of, releasing is probably a good call, if that's what you feel

Hitting the emotional wall doesn't necessarily mean releasing is right: sometimes the best call is to keep retaining and lean into those emotions, feel them, sit with them, meditate, go for a walk; don't resist them, be with them
There is "not a one size fits all approach" to the emotional wall in retention: every individual and every moment is unique

At the emotional wall in retention, with intention, patience, grace for yourself, discipline and commitment, ask whether something clearly has been eating at you for a while and this is a positive opportunity to let it go. If so, go for it: set the intention

At the emotional wall in retention, if nothing clearly has been eating at you for a while to let go of, most of the time, keep retaining: especially earlier in the journey, a big part of retention is pushing up against that edge, a little farther and farther

Even so, don't beat yourself up if or when you release: it's never a bad thing, always part of the journey and a learning experience, even if you might learn, having felt a little sort of on that edge and gone for it anyway, to be a little more disciplined next time
In retention, you will face these emotional walls

A promise: 10-plus years into the retention journey, emotional walls still come up, in different ways, layers, depths and time frames, because this is how we function. "And it ought to still come up."
Emotional walls still coming up in retention is a good thing: you're tuning into deeper levels of yourself
The emotional wall may be uncomfortable, new or unwanted, but go with the roller coaster, the climbs and drops, as long as you keep stepping with awareness, intention and heart
A lot of guys, it seems, start retention, probably personally too, from a little more of a superficial place, so to speak: maybe improving erection quality, or maybe shame
For most guys in the beginning, there's not really a sense that retention is "actually a journey of self-exploration on very deep levels"
Retention is "actually a journey of self-exploration on very deep levels", and it's all beautiful
